test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The average marks of 30 students in a mathematics test were found to be 55. However, it was later discovered that a mark of 72 was mistakenly recorded as 27, and another mark of 64 was mistakenly recorded as 46. What is the actual average score?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Net change** in marks = (Correct marks) − (Incorrect marks)

Net change = (72 + 64) − (27 + 46) = 136 − 73 = **+63**

Average **deviation** = 63 ÷ 30 = **2.1**

Actual Average = Initial Average + Deviation = 55 + 2.1 = **57.1**

**∴ The correct answer is 57.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 30, Initial average = 55, Errors = (27 instead of 72) and (46 instead of 64).

**Formula:** Correct Average = (Correct Sum of Observations) ÷ (Number of Observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53e85f48d4c92c8f38581de3fc2d71ba131eadadd27641d2f8e7c1e9d33604a6.png] 

⇒ Initial Total Marks = 30 × 55 = 1650

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1650 − (27 + 46) + (72 + 64)

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1650 − 73 + 136

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1713

⇒ Actual Average = 1713 ÷ 30

⇒ Actual Average = 57.1

**∴ The correct answer is 57.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Average (Arithmetic Mean)

If every observation in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value **k**, the new average will also increase or decrease by **k**.

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always **zero**. This principle helps in quickly finding missing values or correcting errors.

Weighted Average

When two or more groups are combined, the combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where **n** is the count and **x** is the average of each group.</p
